missing: Measured switchover times on real gaming PCs under load, meaning which current stations kept a high-wattage PC from rebooting in a pull-the-plug test, with prices and a direct pick.
why: The only major reviewer is Popular Mechanics, which appears twice because Yahoo republished it. It gives a general explanation and says outright that it hasn't tested any power station as a UPS. Only one niche site (Outlet Powered) lists models with their switchover times, and those are the makers' own figures, not measurements. The rest are generic explainers, a listicle, a brand blog, a page about runtime rather than switchover, and four pages with no readable text. No source names stations tested with a gaming PC, so a focused comparison of measured switchover times would stand out.
